name: Bikini Kill
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Four people from Olympia, three records in a year, and one deodorant joke that ended up on Nirvana's biggest song.

eras.title: Olympia, before the noise
eras.text: Three Evergreen State College friends, a sandwich shop, a gallery and a pile of zines. Everything Bikini Kill became was homemade first, in a small town where a band could also be a publishing house.

years.src: Olympia Music History Project · SPIN · Wikipedia
years.h: Hanna opens the Reko Muse gallery
years.p: Kathleen Hanna, Tammy Rae Carland and Heidi Arbogast start Reko Muse, an art and performance space in Olympia, Washington. Hanna had already been pulled into spoken word at Evergreen by [[Slim Moon|602432a1-35ce-40ef-90e8-c4a123d438bf]].
years.xp: According to the Olympia Music History Project, Hanna co-founded the gallery in 1988. The SPIN oral history says it hosted all-ages shows, and Wikipedia says it grew out of a photo exhibit about sexism and violence that Evergreen censored.

years.h: Tobi Vail meets Kathi Wilcox over sandwiches
years.p: [[Tobi Vail|0a5c5a29-5bcd-4a8b-9ec0-b0c4d2e28851]] and [[Kathi Wilcox|4a0dd24b-bd17-44e0-bb0c-90238a71c720]] work together at a sandwich shop in Olympia. Vail is also putting out her zine Jigsaw, which is about girls in bands.
years.xp: SPIN's oral history dates the sandwich-shop meeting to 1989; Wikipedia dates Jigsaw to the same year. Vail had been a DJ at Evergreen's KAOS radio and played in the Go Team with K Records' Calvin Johnson before any of this.

years.cap: Bikini Kill performing live at Sylvester Park in Olympia, Washington on May 1... · Wikimedia
years.h: Three friends start Bikini Kill in Olympia
years.p: [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]], Tobi Vail and Kathi Wilcox form the band in October 1990. The name comes from a one-off act by Olympia musician Lois Maffeo, who moved on to another band and left it free.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits Vail with taking the name from Maffeo, who had used it once in the late 1980s, inspired by the 1967 B-movie The Million Eyes of Sumuru. Guitarist [[Billy Karren|7ebf8b8d-9b55-4baa-9eb7-bf8ab4be285d]] completes the four-piece; sources differ on whether he was there from the start or arrived a few months before the first US tour.

By SPIN's account the trio played their first shows in late 1990 or early 1991.

eras.title: Girl Night and a cassette
eras.text: One year in, Bikini Kill are a live band with a cassette, a zine, a label about to be born down the road and a summer trip to Washington, D.C. that helps start a movement with a name.

years.h: Kill Rock Stars opens for business in Olympia
years.p: Slim Moon and Tinuviel Sampson found Kill Rock Stars, the label that will release every Bikini Kill record. Moon said he just wanted to put out his friends' records.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the founding to February 1991. The label later became home to [[Sleater-Kinney|e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7]], Elliott Smith, The Decemberists and Unwound, but Bikini Kill were the release that put it in the national press.

years.h: Hanna writes a deodorant joke on Kurt Cobain's wall
years.p: After a night of drinking, [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] scrawled "Kurt Smells Like Teen Spirit" on [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]]'s wall. It was a joke about a deodorant she and Tobi Vail had seen, and it became the title of [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s biggest song.
years.xp: Hanna tells it in her memoir, as reported by NPR: she wrote it in marker while drunk, and Cobain later asked permission to use it. Wikipedia's account of the song says Cobain did not learn the deodorant was a product until months after the single came out, and had read it as a revolutionary slogan. Vail, who briefly dated Cobain beginning in July 1990, was with Hanna when they found the deodorant.

years.h: Revolution Girl Style Now · the self-released demo tape
years.p: Eight songs on cassette, recorded at Yoyo Studios in Olympia and sold by the band. It is the only Bikini Kill record made before the media got involved.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the tape was recorded at Yoyo Studios across 1990-91 and runs 21 minutes and 29 seconds. The title was a slogan the band used in summer 1991 on the road to D.C. The tape was reissued on vinyl, CD and digital in 2015 by Bikini Kill Records with three bonus tracks.

years.h: Bikini Kill and Bratmobile drive to D.C. for a meeting
years.p: The two Olympia bands head to Washington, D.C., where Hanna and Jenny Toomey organize the first riot grrrl meeting at the Positive Force house in Arlington, Virginia. Hanna also works on a zine with [[Bratmobile|d6dfbc0b-d737-49df-be8e-517b85985bcb]] members.
years.xp: Wikipedia's riot grrrl article describes the meeting as aimed at sexism in the punk scene. The zine is called Riot Grrrl. This is the trip on which the slogan for the demo tape took shape.

years.cap: Kathleen Hanna with Bikini Kill (photo by Denis Gray) · Wikimedia
years.h: Girl Night at the International Pop Underground Convention
years.p: Bikini Kill play the all-female Girl Night bill at K Records' convention in Olympia, alongside Bratmobile and [[Heavens to Betsy|8716a313-c6df-440c-9b74-370e8d79728e]].
years.xp: The convention ran August 20 to 25, 1991. Wikipedia says the night brought together zine writers who had only known each other by mail and phone.

eras.title: Ian MacKaye hits record
eras.text: The band's first real record is produced by the singer of Fugazi. It also brings the first wave of press, much of it hostile, and Hanna's answer to it.

years.h: Vail, Wilcox and Karren start The Frumpies
years.p: With Molly Neuman of Bratmobile, Tobi Vail, Kathi Wilcox and Billy Karren form [[The Frumpies|02231403-76b1-4a4c-accc-714eda94566f]] as a side project.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the group toured as late as the early 2000s, including shows with the Italian punk band Dada Swing.

years.h: Bikini Kill EP · produced by Ian MacKaye
years.p: Six songs and fifteen minutes, made at Inner Ear in Arlington, Virginia with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] producing. Released October 9, 1992 on Kill Rock Stars.
years.xp: SPIN's oral history says the songs were recorded on the spur of the moment at MacKaye's urging, the Dischord Records connection that brought the band to the D.C. area. The tracks are "Double Dare Ya", "Liar", "Carnival", "Suck My Left One", "Feels Blind" and "Thurston Hearts the Who". Wikipedia says the EP was recorded across 1991-92.

years.h: Rolling Stone calls the EP "yowling and moronic"
years.p: According to Wikipedia's riot grrrl article, Rolling Stone dismissed the debut with those words. It was typical of the early press.
years.xp: Hanna's answer was a self-declared media blackout, around 1992 by Wikipedia's riot grrrl article, so girls could speak for themselves without being misrepresented. Wikipedia's Bikini Kill article puts the call to 1994. Rolling Stone later reviewed the 2012 reissue too.

eras.title: London, Joan Jett and the anthem
eras.text: Bikini Kill cross the Atlantic, meet a hero and finish their first album. Three records land within a year.

years.h: Bikini Kill and Huggy Bear tour the UK
years.p: The first UK dates are a co-headline run with [[Huggy Bear|9cf16514-25d6-46c2-8cc8-a8e857e7a3f2]], filmed by Lucy Thane as It Changed My Life: Bikini Kill in the UK.
years.xp: Thane's 30-minute film shows live footage, interviews and the Raincoats and Sister George in kitchens and club bathrooms. Huggy Bear had been thrown out of the Channel 4 show The Word on February 14, 1993 after a protest, and Melody Maker compared it to the Sex Pistols' Bill Grundy incident.

years.h: Yeah Yeah Yeah Yeah · the split with Huggy Bear
years.p: Bikini Kill take one side, Huggy Bear the other (Our Troubled Youth). It came out March 8, 1993 on Catcall and Kill Rock Stars and holds the first recording of "Rebel Girl".

years.h: Joan Jett produces "New Radio" and "Rebel Girl"
years.p: [[Joan Jett|f376828a-b438-4fda-bb2e-dcd5fbe81f83]] plays guitar, sings and produces a new single for the band. Hanna later co-wrote songs on Jett's Pure and Simple.
years.xp: Hanna has called Jett's music an early example of the riot grrrl aesthetic. The three songs Jett produced later opened the 1998 compilation The Singles.

years.cap: Kathleen Hanna with Bikini Kill (photo by Denis Gray) · Wikimedia
years.h: "Rebel Girl" becomes the song everyone knows
years.p: [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] wrote the lyrics and all four members share credit. Wikipedia says it was inspired by artist Juliana Luecking.
years.xp: Three studio versions exist: the split with Huggy Bear, the Joan Jett single, and the album take engineered by Stuart Hallerman. Rolling Stone ranked it 296 on its 2021 list of the greatest songs.

years.h: Pussy Whipped · the first album
years.p: The debut LP on Kill Rock Stars, engineered by Stuart Hallerman, opens the band's first year of national attention.

eras.title: Thrown things, last records
eras.text: Riot grrrl is now a headline and a punchline, and the band lives on stages where people throw things. Two more records, then the end.

years.h: The CD Version of the First Two Records
years.p: Kill Rock Stars pairs the EP and Yeah Yeah Yeah Yeah on one disc.

years.h: "People were throwing chains at our heads"
years.p: Hanna says the hate was real: audiences threw things, and she has said the band was vilified in the 1990s.
years.xp: In Wikipedia's account Hanna said people hated them and that it was very hard to be in the band; she later said the history has mostly written this out. In her memoir she writes that every night was a different set of threatened angry men.

years.h: Two singles, one recording session left
years.p: Kill Rock Stars releases the 7-inches "The Anti-Pleasure Dissertation" and "I Like Fucking". Both later land on The Singles.

years.h: The band records Reject All American with John Goodmanson
years.p: Producer John Goodmanson records the band's second album in November 1995.

years.h: Reject All American · the last album
years.p: Released April 5, 1996 on Kill Rock Stars: twelve songs in under twenty-seven minutes.
years.xp: Robert Christgau said Hanna and Karren added definition and confidence. Rolling Stone ranks it 19 on its 2026 list of the 100 greatest punk albums.

years.big: We lost the ability to talk to each other
q: We were so busy just protecting ourselves.
years.h: The end of the band
years.p: Bikini Kill break up in 1997 after seven years.
years.xp: Hanna told ABC News that they were so busy protecting themselves from people throwing things at them that the band could no longer talk to each other. Vail has said social media would have ended it in three months. Some listings give 1998 as the final year.

eras.title: Everybody scatters
eras.text: The members split into new bands and their own projects. The records stay in print but the band is mostly a memory until the mid-2010s.

years.h: The Singles · nine tracks, the Jett sessions on top
years.p: Released June 23, 1998, gathering the 1993 and 1995 single sides in 17 minutes. Pitchfork raised its rating to 10 on the 2018 reissue.

years.h: Hanna leaves for [[Le Tigre|2d67239c-aa40-4ad5-a807-9052b66857a6]]
years.p: After a solo record on a $40 drum machine, Hanna forms Le Tigre with Johanna Fateman and Sadie Benning.
years.xp: The solo album, Julie Ruin, later gave its name to her post-Le Tigre band [[The Julie Ruin|357ffd02-384f-4dbd-abcd-5f1bcb616ef9]], in which Wilcox played bass.

years.h: Tobi Vail co-founds Ladyfest
years.p: Vail is one of the founders of Ladyfest in 2000 and later plays in Spider and the Webs and The Old Haunts.

years.h: Hanna leaves Le Tigre because of illness
years.p: Hanna leaves the band that year; the illness was later diagnosed as Lyme disease.
years.xp: NPR reported that the undiagnosed Lyme disease kept her from performing for a stretch. She returned after treatment.

years.h: Hanna starts Bikini Kill Records
years.p: She launches the label to reissue the catalog, saying a kind of 90s feminism revival prompted it.

eras.title: Taking the catalog back
eras.text: Documentaries, reissues and a viral clip put the band back in view, and the band gets the rights to its music.

years.h: The Punk Singer tells Hanna's story
years.p: Sini Anderson's documentary covers Hanna's career including the Lyme disease diagnosis.

years.h: Revolution Girl Style Now finally reissued
years.p: The demo tape comes out on vinyl, CD and digital, with bonus tracks "Ocean Song", "Just Once" and "Playground".

years.h: Tobi Vail files a copyright claim on the Clinton clip
years.p: A pro-Hillary Clinton video set to "Rebel Girl" goes viral after John Podesta tweets it. Vail files a notice and it comes down.
years.xp: Vail said the band doesn't authorize use of its songs in advertisements. Vail supported Bernie Sanders in the primary.

years.h: Three of them play one song at The Kitchen
years.p: Hanna, Wilcox and Vail perform at a New York book-release event for Jenn Pelly's book on The Raincoats.

years.h: The whole catalog hits streaming
years.p: Everything is on Apple Music and Spotify, and The Singles is reissued on CD and vinyl.

eras.title: The room is full now
eras.text: The reunion has a new guitarist and none of the old fear. The crowds are bigger than they ever were in the 1990s.

years.h: Reunion at the Hollywood Palladium
years.p: Announced January 15, the first show is April 25 at the Palladium with Alice Bag opening. Erica Dawn Lyle plays guitar in place of [[Billy Karren|7ebf8b8d-9b55-4baa-9eb7-bf8ab4be285d]].
years.xp: Rolling Stone lists the New York dates as Brooklyn Steel on May 31 and Terminal 5 on June 1. Its story does not say why Karren was not part of it; Wikipedia says he did not take part.

years.h: Two European dates, Brixton Academy included
years.p: The band plays London at Brixton Academy, supported by Big Joanie, The Tuts and Child's Pose.

years.h: Bikini Kill headline day three of Riot Fest in Chicago
years.p: Riot Fest on September 15 puts the band on a festival main stage.

years.h: A 2020 tour is announced, then the pandemic hits
years.p: Thirteen North American dates were to begin March 13, 2020 at the Capitol Theater in Olympia; the tour was moved to 2022.

years.h: Sara Landeau takes over on guitar
years.p: Landeau, who has played with Hanna and Wilcox in The Julie Ruin, becomes the touring guitarist.

years.h: First Australian tour in 26 years
years.p: Vail became ill during the tour and Lauren Hammel, the band's Australian drum tech and a member of Tropical Fuck Storm, played drums at the Victorian shows.

years.h: Hanna publishes her memoir and the band tours the UK
years.p: Rebel Girl: My Life as a Feminist Punk is published by Harper Collins; a UK tour begins June 12.

sources.title: SPIN: oral history of the Bikini Kill EP
